title: Unchanged test-run rescans redo history-sized compaction selection and republish state under the commit lock
outcome: An idle test-run rescan with no changes no longer rebuilds the whole compaction population or republishes state while it holds the src/test_runs.rs:1126 commit lock. Compaction selection (A) and the publish step (B) land as separate candidates, A first. Live idle-backstop rescans hold that lock 371/460/686 ms (min/median/max), of which compaction selection takes 173-315 ms and the publish step 116-270 ms (w-e2972bb21221 note 09f9687e).
acceptance: (A) An unchanged rescan does no compaction selection; a changed eligibility input, including each one the source list finds, is still compacted on the next pass.
(B) An unchanged rescan neither advances the state revision nor republishes, or else RED-B shows that this cost doesn't exist and B is dropped with that evidence.
The review pair is clean and the full gate passes on the exact landed tree.
A post-landing live trace is reported, with the cold first scan kept separate from idle passes, and without claiming the parent's live criterion.
